correctness.rationale: The 3D period-two equations are bijective with the 1D cubic period-two equations only on cycles. Factoring their sum and difference gives an exact 0/1/3 census. The positive and negative Jacobians are conjugate by diag(1,-1,1), so the return derivative is the square of a matrix with characteristic polynomial λ³−λ²+2s; its root factorization proves the golden boundary and unstable dimensions. On extra cycles UV=−1 gives determinant 4. Verified with 164 exact symbolic/radical identities over ten rational representatives; the proof, not the experiments, establishes the quantified real-parameter theorem.

value.rationale: The exact three-dimensional stability window strictly precedes the scalar-cubic flip boundary and the creation of two more cycles, revealing a genuine transverse-instability effect invisible to the cubic orbit count. A whole-positive-parameter 0/1/3 census and determinant-four obstruction close a natural analytic gap in the original numerical bifurcation investigation; the precise threshold discriminates the existence of local period-two sinks.
